newsitem.title: USA: N. Dakota rains impede harvest, aid soil moisture.
newsitem.headline: N. Dakota rains impede harvest, aid soil moisture.

text.p: Rains disrupted North Dakota's harvest in the week ended Sunday but the precipitation also replenished low soil moisture levels, the state's agricultural statistics service said.
Corn was four percent harvested as of Sunday, trailing the average of 10 percent. Soybeans were 25 percent harvested, against the 32 percent average.
Corn was rated 17 percent poor, 30 percent fair, 43 percent good and 10 percent excellent.
Soybeans were rated 30 percent poor, 30 percent fair, 36 percent good and four percent excellent.
Blackbirds continued to be a problem in some sunflower fields while grasshoppers were reported in the south.
Sunflowers were rated three percent poor, 19 percent fair 58 percent good and 20 percent excellent.
Sugarbeets were 10 percent lifted, against the 13 percent average. The crop was rated five percent poor, 15 percent fair, 73 percent good and seven percent excellent.
Topsoil moisture was rated two percent very short, 15 percent short, 77 percent adequate and six percent surplus.
